hypothesis: Wave D17 (C_L3_MACH_FRAME_DRAGGING): rotating matter drags local inertial frames. Its weak-field part, the gravitomagnetic precession G/(c^2 r^3) [3 (J.r) r - J] averaged on a polar orbit, predicts that the Gravity Probe B gyroscopes drift east-west at G J cos(delta)/(2 c^2 a^3) = 39.17 mas/yr (computed before the comparison is read).

observable.quantity: frame-dragging drift rate of the GP-B gyroscopes (east-west, relative to the guide star IM Pegasi)
observable.domain: Gravity Probe B, polar orbit at 642 km, 2004-2005 science data, final result of Everitt et al. (2011) PRL 106, 221101 (arXiv:1105.3456)

prediction_method.description: Orbit average of the gravitomagnetic precession sampled on a circular polar orbit (general path, equals the closed form to 1e-15), projected on the gyroscope pointing at the guide star. Measured value and 1-sigma transcribed after approval from the paper's abstract/table as published. The script refuses to run unless this card is APPROVED and the data sha256 matches.

fixed_parameters: Earth polar moment C = 8.034e37 kg m^2, rotation 7.292115e-5 rad/s (literature, AI choice)
orbit circular, polar, altitude 642 km above R_E = 6378.137 km
thresholds 2 and 3 sigma of the published measurement (AI choice)
fail_criterion: FAILED if |prediction - measurement| > 3 sigma. INCONCLUSIVE in between.
note: Disclosure: the drafter has not opened the paper for this card, but recalls from general knowledge that GP-B confirmed frame dragging at about the 20 percent level close to the GR value of about 39 mas/yr; a PASS is therefore expected and the test is weak. It tests the weak-field gravitomagnetic term behind D17, not the shell's strong-field Brill-Cohen formula, and it is a test of GR, not of anything UET-distinct. The reading of frame dragging as 'matter decides what not rotating means' is an AI interpretation (C_L3_MACH_FRAME_DRAGGING note). Orbit altitude and Earth's moment are AI-chosen literature values; a 0.3 percent change in a moves the prediction by 1 percent, far below the measurement error. Approved by the author in chat on 2026-11-24 as drafted ("Approve and run"); this approval is committed before the comparison data are downloaded or read.
